title: Per-tenant SLO / Cost Tradeoffs + Synthetic Traffic Playbook — Arch review notes
content:
Meeting: Per-tenant SLO vs cost tradeoffs + synthetic traffic playbook (architecture review)
Date: 2024-11-06 10:00 PT
Attendees: Priya Nambiar (owner), Evan Rodriguez, Kai Zhao, Maya Patel, Liam O'Connor, notes: Zoe Hernandez (observer)
Goals for this session:
- Align on proposed per-tenant SLO model and billing/crediting implications.
- Review synthetic traffic playbook for safe rollout and capacity validation.
- Lock down guardrails for cost vs latency tiering and what we expose to customers.

Background / short context:
- Customers increasingly request per-tenant SLOs (p99 latency at Xms, or throughput guarantees) for Dedicated and Private.
- Providing SLOs implies resource reservation/crediting, capacity commit rules, and metrics surface.
- We currently have global SLOs and tenant QoS credits (prototype). Need an operational model that ties SLOs to cost and a deterministic rollout/test plan (synthetic traffic) before change is allowed.

Summary of proposals presented (three options):
1) Soft-tiered SLOs (recommended baseline)
   - Offer Bronze/Silver/Gold SLO tiers mapped to latency targets and a soft credit pool.
   - Runtime: preferential scheduling in slot allocator, best-effort preemption with notifications.
   - Billing: small surcharge + flexible commit; customer can exceed but will receive degraded QoS without hard failures.
   - Upside: simple, low ops overhead.
   - Downside: unpredictable tail behavior under extreme contended events.

2) Hard-reserved capacity per-tenant (strict isolation)
   - Allocate dedicated GPU slots/pools to tenant up to their reserved capacity. Hard admission control; reject beyond reservation.
   - Billing: fixed reservation fee + overage pricing disabled.
   - Upside: deterministic SLO guarantees.
   - Downside: cost inefficiency, fragmentation, higher capex.

3) Hybrid dynamic reservation with elastic burst buckets
   - Baseline reserved capacity with ephemeral burst tokens drawn from a shared burst pool. Tokens priced at higher per-token cost. Automated reclaiming.
   - Runtime complexity: token broker + accounting; requires changes to routing and billing pipelines.
   - Upside: balances efficiency and predictability.
   - Downside: more operational complexity and engineering effort.

Engineering tradeoffs discussed:
- Isolation vs utilization: strict reservations give SLAs but kill bin-packing benefits; soft tiers risk noisy neighbor impact.
- Observability requirements: to safely operate soft/hybrid tiers we need per-request tenant labels carried across the stack and precise p95/p99 sketches (HDR histograms, reservoir for tails).
- Billing alignment: to avoid revenue leakage we must correlate throttling events with billing decisions (ticket PLAT-3421).
- Routing & preemption: preemption should be graceful — return a standard error code plus a retry-backoff hint and optional fallback to lower-tier model variant.

Decisions made (consensus):
- Adopt option 3 (Hybrid dynamic reservation with elastic burst buckets) as primary for Dedicated customers, phased rollout. Rationale: best balance for enterprise customers who need predictability but we must preserve utilization.
- Implement a simplified form initially: baseline reservation + a small shared burst pool (PoC). Full token broker deferred.
- Expose three visible SLO tiers to customers (silver/gold/platinum) — internal mapping to reservation + burst allowances documented in product contract.
- Synthetic traffic playbook will be required for any rollout that touches reservation/burst logic. Playbook must be codified in repo and include canary traffic profiles, spike scenarios, and teardown steps.

Playbook outline (actionable checklist) — required before enabling hybrid reservations in a region:
1) Create canary tenant(s) with reservation=R and burst_budget=B in staging.
2) Run baseline synthetic generator (loadgen-v2) for 24h at 60% of R to collect steady-state metrics. Save histograms.
3) Execute 10-minute spike tests (3x, 10x, 30x) to exercise burst pool; each spike followed by 30-minute recovery. Capture p50/p95/p99 and error rates.
4) Run mixed-concurrency conversational workloads (simulate long-context sessions to validate KV cache behavior).
5) Validate cost counters: per-token GPU usage, memory residency, KV cache hit/miss; ensure billing pipeline PLAT-3499 records token consumption for bursts.
6) Canary to production gating: automated checks require: p99 <= target + 20% for target tier, error_rate <= 0.1% for golden, no eviction-induced OOMs, no sustained queue growth.
7) Rollback/teardown steps documented: stop all load generators, drain sessions, revoke burst budget policy, and run postmortem trace.

Instrumentation / telemetry requirements (short list):
- Tenant label propagated on every RPC (internal header X-Tenant-ID).
- Per-tenant rolling HDR histograms for latency (1m/5m/1h windows).
- Burst token accounting metric exposed (tenant.tokens.used, tenant.tokens.left).
- Alerts: burst_pool_utilization > 80% sustained for 10m, tenant_queue_growth_rate > threshold, p99 regression > 30% vs baseline.

Open technical risks and unresolved questions:
- Token broker complexity: who owns the ledger? Options: centralized service (single point of failure) vs sharded per-region ledger. (Action: Kai to prototype a sharded ledger model — due 2024-11-20)
- Billing reconciliation lag: current billing pipeline is eventual; need near-real-time counters for accurate overage charging. (Action: Evan to scope PLAT-3499 integration with billing ingest)
- Noisy neighbor detection: what heuristics automatically classify noisy tenants vs systemic infra issues? (Action: Maya to draft heuristic set and initial thresholds)
- Safety during burst exhaustion: what fallback model variants are acceptable for customer apps? (Action: Product to provide mapping table)

Simulation notes (quick results from PoC sim run):
- PoC parameters: R=1000 tokens/s, shared_burst_pool=2000 tokens/s, 24h baseline then spike tests.
- Observed utilization: baseline 62% avg, burst_pool peaked at 74% during 3x spikes, average p99 increased from 210ms -> 270ms during 10x spike, error rate spiked to 0.08% for platinum tenants (acceptable per draft).
- Memory/residency: KV cache hit-rate dropped from 88%->76% during sustained spikes; this increased per-token cost by ~12% in the worst window.

Action items (owners and due dates):
- Kai Zhao: Prototype sharded burst ledger and simple eviction policy (due 2024-11-20).
- Evan Rodriguez: Billing integration spec for near-real-time counters + test harness (PLAT-3499) (due 2024-11-15).
- Maya Patel: Noisy-neighbor heuristics doc and alert thresholds (due 2024-11-12).
- Priya Nambiar: Draft customer-facing SLO tier mapping & contract language and update Confluence (due 2024-11-10).
- Liam O'Connor: Add synthetic traffic playbook to infra repo (infra/playbooks/synthetic-slo-tests.md) and implement the automated gating checks (due 2024-11-18).

Notes / informal items captured during discussion (raw):
- "We should avoid hard-reservations for < $10k ARR customers" — quick product note, not a formal decision.
- Zoe: "Consider cheapest fallback variant being a 4-bit quantized model with degraded output quality but preserved latency" — flagged for product quality evaluation.
- Several references to previous experiments (see GH PR / infra loadgen history).

Next review session:
- 2024-11-20 10:00 PT: review Kai's prototype + first billing ingest test results.

Attachments/where to find artifacts:
- Load generator configs: infra/loadgen/canary/hybrid-resv-config.yml (branch: feat/hybrid-reservations)
- PoC simulation results: s3://redwood-test-results/hybrid-resv/poc-2024-11-05-hdr.json
- Draft SLO mapping: Confluence Per-Tenant SLO Strategy (linked above)

End notes: keep this doc as the working source for the rollout. Move to final when the PoC passes gating checks and product copy is finalized.
